high_config.portrait: When a demand is unclear but allows you to choose a method, you turn it into something people can inspect: a draft, sample, process, or finished piece. You use feedback to improve the work, then decide what should happen next instead of waiting for every step to be assigned. The result is practical initiative, not just activity: your judgment helps shape both the work and its next use. The chart supports this pattern through a somewhat strong Ji Earth Day Master, with Eating God as its leading influence at 9 and Companion at 8. Eating God appears openly as Xin on the month stem, while Ji appears on the hour stem. These are structural tendencies, not proof that every setting will reward your work.
observable_signals: A colleague gives you a broad request, and you return with a sample or working draft rather than only a list of questions. You point to what is already usable, ask which part needs changing, and revise against that response. In a meeting, you bring discussion back to a concrete version people can inspect. Eating God leads at 9 and appears as Xin on the month stem; the somewhat strong Ji Earth Day Master gives this output a firm base. After a trial or first delivery reveals a gap, you identify a practical next step and start it without needing someone to map every move. low_config.portrait: When the request stays vague and no one defines acceptance, ownership, or reuse, you can fill in the missing terms by producing more work. A draft becomes extra revisions; a completed task becomes an unspoken agreement to take the next one. You keep the work moving, but the scope and return remain unsettled. The key leak is not that making things is inherently costly. It is that finished work becomes your way to prove usefulness before you have negotiated what the work is for. The chart’s Eating God at 9 and Seven Killings at 5 support the demand-to-output pattern; the Wealth influences total 1, with Indirect Wealth at 1 and Direct Wealth at 0. These weights point to a structural emphasis, not a fixed limit on reward.
observable_signals: A requester asks for a small change, but you make the change and add improvements that were not requested. You do not pause to ask whether the extra work changes the deadline, the definition of done, or who owns the next step. The result looks helpful, while the agreement remains incomplete. You finish a task and immediately accept the next demand, even though nobody has said whether the first result will be reused, credited, or maintained. If someone asks what is next, you answer with another task rather than first closing the loop on the work already delivered. Companion at 8 supports active judgment, so the low-spec shift is not simply lack of initiative; it is initiative spent before the terms are clear. The Ji Earth Day Master is somewhat strong, and the supplied reading links this structure to choosing next steps. Notice whether that choice includes setting boundaries around the earlier work.

You keep revising because the result has not received a clear response, then treat silence as a reason to make another version. The effort becomes visible, but the acceptance standard remains hidden, so you cannot tell whether the next edit is useful or merely another attempt to secure approval. Seven Killings at 5 and Eating God at 9 support a pattern in which a hard demand gets answered with concrete work. belief.limiting_belief: The belief most likely to grow from this defensive pattern is: 「If I keep delivering, the terms will sort themselves out.」 It can sound practical because making a result is the part you can control immediately. But it turns completion into a substitute for asking what counts as accepted, who owns the next step, and whether the result will be reused or recognized. The chart supports why this belief could take hold: Eating God leads at 9, Seven Killings is 5, and the supplied core loop describes answering hard demands with visible work. belief.origin: The belief can develop through a repeated sequence: a hard demand arrives, you create something tangible, and the immediate problem becomes easier to judge. That response works well enough to invite another request, while the agreement around the first result receives less attention. Because your chart has Eating God at 9 and Companion at 8, making and deciding are strongly represented; Seven Killings at 5 supplies the demand side of the described loop. belief.ceiling_effect: The belief lowers your ceiling by narrowing the work you are willing to take on to whatever you can personally finish and prove. You may spend the time that could go toward a more useful version, a reusable process, or a clear negotiation on unrequested revisions. You also give up information: without asking what decision the result should enable, you cannot know whether another round of work is valuable. The chart places strong emphasis on Eating God at 9 and Companion at 8, with the Ji Earth Day Master marked somewhat strong, so there is support for both producing and choosing. The ceiling falls when production replaces choice, not because the chart sets a fixed maximum.

awareness.key_moment: The track can switch when you notice that the task is no longer mainly about making a good result. It has become a way to get someone else to define acceptance after you have already spent the effort. At that point, pause before the next revision or next assignment and ask what decision the work needs to support. Then make the terms visible: what is complete, who owns what follows, and how the result will be used. This intervention fits the supplied leak directly. Eating God at 9 supports producing a visible result, while the Wealth family totals 1, so defining return and reuse should be deliberate rather than assumed. The chart marks Ji Earth as somewhat strong, but it does not decide when you will notice the pattern.
awareness.what_to_notice: Notice the moment you say yes to more work while the previous result still has no clear acceptance or owner. Ask yourself whether the next action is a chosen improvement or an attempt to make an unstated standard finally appear. Also check whether you can name who will use the finished work and what they will do with it. These are observable questions, not a test of motivation. The supplied core loop names undefined acceptance, next-step ownership, reuse, and payment as the places to clarify. Eating God at 9 and Seven Killings at 5 support why demand can quickly turn into production; the Wealth family total of 1 makes it especially useful to check whether return has been discussed rather than inferred.

You find yourself making a second version mainly because the requester has not responded, rather than because new information showed what needs changing. switch_actions: Before your next substantial task, send a short written note stating the requested result, what will count as accepted, who makes that decision, and who owns the next step. For one task in the coming week, make a small version before expanding it. Show it to the decision-maker and ask which specific requirement it satisfies and what remains missing. Mark any item that has no answer, then ask one direct question the next morning instead of silently filling the gap with more work. This creates a repeatable pause at the loop’s loss point.
